facts.value: Emergency laparoscopy converted to open operation because of purulent fluid and adhesions. A Meckel diverticulum ~40 cm proximal to ileocecal valve contained a biliary stent; its distal end perforated adjacent ileum.
About 20 cm of small bowel, including diverticulum and perforation, was resected with side-to-side anastomosis, irrigation and drainage.

args.rationale: 70-year-old woman who has just had an emergency operation. It began laparoscopically and was converted to open because of purulent peritonitis and adhesions. About 20 cm of small bowel was removed, including a Meckel diverticulum and an ileal perforation caused by a migrated biliary stent. The bowel was rejoined with a side-to-side anastomosis, and the abdomen was irrigated and drained. Her comorbidities (chronic AF, COPD, type 2 diabetes, hypertension) and the purulent contamination put her at high risk of sepsis, respiratory failure, arrhythmia and anastomotic leak. She needs ICU or high-dependency monitoring after surgery.
args.followup_or_handoff: Handoff to ICU and surgical team. 1) Monitor closely: hemodynamics, urine output, and serial lactate and labs (CBC, electrolytes, creatinine, glucose, coagulation). Labs were not available before surgery, so there is no baseline. 2) No antibiotic order was recorded in this encounter. Start broad-spectrum IV antibiotics for secondary peritonitis as soon as allergies are confirmed, and send the intraoperative peritoneal fluid for culture. 3) Medications, anticoagulant use for AF, and allergies are not documented and must be confirmed. Plan when to restart anticoagulation, with VTE prophylaxis in the meantime. 4) Keep her nil by mouth with nasogastric decompression. Give IV fluids, control glucose with insulin, control AF rate, and provide COPD care with bronchodilators and chest physiotherapy. 5) Watch drain output and for signs of anastomotic leak or abscess. 6) Find out why she had a biliary stent and when it was placed (stones or malignancy). The stent has migrated, so the biliary tree now has no stent. Check liver function tests and arrange a gastroenterology/ERCP review for biliary drainage. 7) Send the resected specimen for histopathology.
